newsitem.title: UK: BBC says licence deal leaves financial challenges.
newsitem.headline: BBC says licence deal leaves financial challenges.

text.p: The BBC said on Wednesday that the five-year licence fee settlement announced by the UK government would leave it with financial challenges to surmount.

"The welcome rise in the licence fee in the early years will enable the BBC to enter the digital age with pioneering new services for all our licence payers. We start those services next October," Director-General John Birt said in a statement.

"But the reductions announced in later years are a disappointment. They will affect the BBC's ability to sustain those services as the digital world develops," he added after the government rejected his call for an above-inflation rise.

The digital television age is expected to begin in Britain next autumn when BSkyB launches a digital satellite service with some 200 channels. Terrestrial digital services -- offering some 35 channels -- are set to begin in mid-1998.
The BBC plans to offer its existing BBC 1 and BBC 2 services in a wide-screen digital format and offer extra programming to all licence-payers with digital receivers.
It plans to provide its programming on all delivery mechanisms -- satellite, terrestrial and cable.
The BBC also has plans to launch digital themed subscription services as part of a partnership with the Flextech pay television group.
"We will do everything we can to secure the future of our services by seeking to improve our efficiency and by building our commercial revenues," Birt added.
He added that the government would need to ensure that digital services for licence fee payers could be maintained into the next century.
National Heritage Secretary Virginia Bottomley unveiled a five-year formula which will leave the licence fee fractionally lower in real terms at the end of the five years.
The increase in the first year will be in line with the Retail Price Index. Above-inflation increases in years two and three will be balanced by lower rises in the last two years.
The BBC has been developing its commercial activities but still derives some 1.8 billion stg -- 95 percent of its revenue -- from the annual licence payable by all television set owners.
The fee stands at 89.50 stg for a colour set. It will rise to 91.50 stg from next April.
